version.changelog: v1.1.0: Added folder management, knowledge association discovery, AI-powered insights, improved semantic search with pgvector

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: knowmine
Version: 1.1.0

The 'knowmine' skill is a remote-hosted MCP server configuration for a personal knowledge base service (knowmine.ai). It provides 11 tools for semantic search, memory persistence, and knowledge management using pgvector. While the skill involves sending user-provided data to a third-party service, this is the explicitly stated purpose, and there are no indicators of malicious intent, obfuscation, or unauthorized data exfiltration in the SKILL.md or _meta.json files.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (a cloud-hosted MCP-backed personal knowledge base) matches the credentials it requests, but provenance is unknown, it will persist user data to a remote service, and the README asks you to run external installers — so verify the service and avoid uploading secrets before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (pgvector-backed personal knowledge base via MCP) aligns with the single required secret (KNOWMINE_API_KEY) and the provided MCP endpoint. However the package has no homepage/source metadata in the registry entry and the owner is an opaque ID — missing provenance increases risk.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is instruction-only and explicitly tells the agent to call a remote MCP endpoint (https://knowmine.ai/api/mcp) using a bearer API key; that behavior is expected for a hosted KB. It also suggests installing via `npx clawhub@latest install knowmine`. The instructions therefore will cause the agent to transmit user-provided content to a third-party cloud service (data persistence). The doc does not warn about avoiding sensitive secrets or describe retention/encryption.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only). The README suggests running `npx clawhub@latest install knowmine`, which downloads and executes code from the network — a standard but non-trivial action. Because there is no package/source metadata listed here, you should verify the npm/package origin and authenticity before running any installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only declared required environment value is KNOWMINE_API_KEY (km_mcp_…), which is proportionate to a hosted MCP service. That key grants access to a hosted account and storage, so it should be treated as sensitive and scoped/rotated appropriately; no unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always and uses normal autonomous invocation. It provides a persistent cloud-backed memory (the intended function) — this increases blast radius because anything you save is stored remotely. The skill does not request modification rights to other skills or system settings, which is good, but persistence of user data on an external service is the primary privilege to consider.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says (a cloud-hosted MCP knowledge base) but provenance is unclear and it will store whatever you send to knowmine.ai. Before installing: (1) verify the vendor/site (knowmine.ai) and that the npm/ClawHub package is official; (2) create a dedicated account/key with the least privileges and test with non-sensitive data; (3) review KnowMine's privacy, storage, retention, and deletion policy and whether data is encrypted at rest; (4) avoid uploading secrets, credentials, or private keys into the knowledge base; (5) be cautious running the suggested `npx clawhub@latest` command — confirm the package identity and contents first; (6) have a plan to rotate/revoke the KNOWMINE_API_KEY if you suspect misuse. If you want a lower-risk alternative, consider a local-only knowledge store rather than a remote-hosted MCP service.
